appearance_facts.fact: A single purple line chart spans the width of the plot, connecting data points for each year from 2012 to 2023.
The line begins at a low vertical position, rises slightly, and then shows a distinct upward peak in 2014.
The line dips downward after the 2014 peak and then trends steadily upward through 2017.
The line reaches a high point in 2018, flattens slightly in 2019, and dips slightly in 2020, remaining well above the starting level.
The line shows a steep, sharp increase from 2020 to 2021, reaching its highest vertical peak in 2022, followed by a slight downward slope in 2023.
The end point of the line in 2023 is positioned significantly higher on the page than the starting point in 2012, indicating a general upward trajectory over the decade.

printed_facts.fact: The title reads: 'Falling Respiratory Infection Cases in Sentinel Sites from 2012 to 2023'.
A subtitle reads: 'Sentinel surveillance record shown in the dashboard summary'.
The axis is labeled 'Respiratory infection cases' with tick marks at 0, 700, 1400, 2100, and 2800.
The axis is labeled 'Year' with tick marks for every year from 2012 to 2023.

public_definitions: The task asks to select the operational route that best fits the overall case pattern.
Options include: 'Route the record to increasing-activity follow-up', 'Route the record to easing-activity follow-up', and 'Route the record to standard surveillance monitoring'.
uncertain: There is a direct contradiction between the chart title, which states 'Falling Respiratory Infection Cases', and the visual data, which shows a line that starts low and ends high (an increase).
It is unclear whether the 'overall case pattern' refers to the entire 12-year span or specifically the most recent trend (2020-2023), though both periods show an upward movement in the visual data.
